title: A customer with a noisy bike
scenario: You work in a bike shop. You took a phone call from a customer. Your colleague Dan repairs the bikes and is not in the shop today. Leave him a short note.

lines.t: Hello, I bought a red bike from you last month.
The front brake is very loud, and the bell does not work.
I am sorry to hear that. Would you like to bring it in?
Yes. I can come on Thursday after work, at about six. Please call my mobile, 555 0142, not my home number.
Fine. My colleague Dan will look at it.
Thank you. By the way, your shop window looks lovely this week!

task.prompt: Write a note to Dan (30–50 words). Say what the customer wants and the details he needs.

points.idea: The brake is noisy and the bell is broken.
The customer brings it on Thursday at about six.

leave_out.idea: The compliment about the shop window.

model: Dan, a customer is bringing her bike in on Thursday at about 6 in the evening. The front brake makes a very loud noise and the bell is broken. Please call her mobile on 555 0142 if you have any questions.
tips: A note for a colleague is a list of facts in sentences: what, when, how to contact. Skip the polite chat from the call.
Copy numbers and times exactly as you heard them. A wrong digit makes the whole note useless.
explain: Dan needs the two problems, the day and time, and the number. He does not need the bike colour or the compliment about the window.
